Policy Statement

Nuclear Waste Services (NWS) is committed to creating an inclusive and safe working environment where people are protected from bullying and harassment, which is critical to the delivery to the NWS vision and values.

NWS has a zero tolerance of bullying and harassment of any kind as defined in this policy, both in the workplace or outside of the workplace in a work-related context and provides an enhanced grievance process for complaints relating to bullying and harassment.

NWS commits to: We will achieve this by:

Acting with integrity Everyone working for NWS will take responsibility for their own behaviour, ensuring that they treat others with respect and dignity.

Bullying and harassment has no place in NWS. Sustaining a culture where everyone feels able to call out or report behaviours they feel is unacceptable to them and to be confident that their concerns will be taken seriously. Ensuring that if employees complain they are being bullied or harassed, then they have a grievance which must be dealt with regardless of whether their complaint accords with a standard definition of bullying and harassment.

Ensuring conduct aligns to the NWS Values and the NDA Code of Conduct Taking into account the NWS Values and NDA Code of Conduct and where relevant, raise awareness of relevant legal protections such as “harassment” related to a “protected characteristic” and “victimisation”.

This policy applies to anyone who works for NWS, whether directly employed by the organisation or not. It also applies to anyone who is in contact with people working NWS in the course of their work including customers, external stakeholders, and visitors.

It applies to bullying or harassment that occurs both in the workplace and outside of the workplace such as on business trips, client or supplier events, or work-related social events. This also includes the inappropriate use of all social media even when this originates outside of work.

This policy does not form part of any contract, including any contract of employment and NWS may amend it at any time.

Definitions

NWS recognise that part of working life includes constructive feedback and appropriate performance management discussions which can sometimes result in differences of opinion, conflicts and tension between individuals, but NWS has a zero-tolerance approach to bullying and harassment of any kind and defines bullying as:

Any unwanted behaviour that makes someone feel intimidated, degraded, humiliated, or offended. It is unwelcome, unwarranted behaviour that causes a detrimental effect on an individual or group through means that undermines, humiliates, excludes and/or denigrates the recipient.

It is not necessarily always obvious or apparent to others and may happen in the workplace without an employer’s awareness. Bullying and harassment can be between two individuals, or it may involve groups of people. It may take place over a period of time, but can also occur as a single, offensive act.

It is important to understand that unlawful behaviour may, in some circumstances, give rise to the possibility of personal liability for those found to have acted unlawfully. There may also be circumstances in which behaviour constitutes a potential criminal offence and in such cases the NWS may consider referring concerns to the Police.

The Equality Act defines harassment as:

Unwanted conduct related to a relevant protected characteristic, which has the purpose or effect of violating an individual’s dignity or of creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment for that individual.

Examples of bullying include but are not limited to:

behaviour causing humiliation or offence whether this is the intention or not and whether this takes place in private or in front of others

humiliating someone by making comments about their social background, personal appearance, or heritage

undermining a worker with persistent criticism

overbearing supervision or otherwise misuse of power or position

gossip or making defamatory comments

shouting

isolation / exclusion (physical or social)

name calling or insults

intimidatory or oppressive behaviour

excessive, unjustified monitoring of work

unfairly removing duties or responsibilities or withholding information or resources

delivering performance feedback in an inappropriate manner, time and/or place

intentionally blocking progression or preventing training and development opportunities

Examples of harassment include but are not limited to:

jokes, or ‘banter’ and comments, based on race, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender, religious belief or similar belief, marital status, or trans status regardless of the intent of the person making the jokes or taking part in the ‘banter’

displaying or sending inappropriate or offensive pictures, posters, or written material

displaying or sending offensive images or messages online

the impact of jokes and comments as witnessed by others

Sexual Harassment

The Equality Act also defines sexual harassment as:

Unwanted conduct or a sexual nature which has the purpose or effect of violating a person’s dignity or of creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment for a person.

This includes subjecting someone to unwanted conduct of a sexual nature, when related to sex or gender reassignment, if that unwanted conduct has the purpose or effect of violating the employee’s dignity and/or creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment for the employee, and the employee is treated less favourably because they submitted to, or rejected, the unwanted conduct.

Examples of sexual harassment include but are not limited to:

sexual comments or jokes

unwanted advances or propositions

intrusive questions about a person’s private or sex life or a person discussing their own sex life
